correctness.rationale: For the stipulated probability objective, absolute inclination cosine is uniform on [0,1] and phase is uniform modulo π. Open equal-length phase arcs leave uncovered length Σ(g_j−ell)_+, so Jensen proves global optimality for each inclination. When c≤a_n, at the inclination where ell=π/n every unequal vector leaves positive uncovered length, and continuity gives strict loss on an interval of positive measure, also at c=a_n. When c>a_n, continuity at edge-on inclination gives precisely the plateau max g_j≤2 arcsin(c). In the incomplete regime the boundary term in integration by parts vanishes at z_0=sqrt(a_n²−c²)/a_n; the positive integral has leading term 2nc z_0³/(3πτ). Using z_0∼sqrt(2u_n(τ−u_n))/a_n gives the stated coefficient; the indicated substitution gives the exact arctangents. The count uses the n=2 precedent and n=1 cannot be complete at positive IWA. The frozen proof's pointwise-coverage wording must be read as a statement about phase measure: strict detection leaves isolated misses at equality gaps, including at the critical uniform calendar. A guarantee for every configuration instead requires max g_j<2 arcsin(c); the stated probability-one criterion is correct. The supplied checker and VERIFICATION.md were read but not executed; their numerical diagnostics are not the basis of the proof.
